label: Immer

text.BHSA JER 20:1: וַיִּשְׁמַ֤ע פַּשְׁחוּר֙ בֶּן־אִמֵּ֣ר הַכֹּהֵ֔ן וְהֽוּא־פָקִ֥יד נָגִ֖יד בְּבֵ֣ית יְהוָ֑ה אֶֽת־יִרְמְיָ֔הוּ נִבָּ֖א אֶת־הַדְּבָרִ֥ים הָאֵֽלֶּה׃
text.KJV JER 20:1: Now Pashur the son of Immer the priest, who was also chief governor in the house of the LORD, heard that Jeremiah prophesied these things.
text.BHSA JER 20:2: וַיַּכֶּ֣ה פַשְׁח֔וּר אֵ֖ת יִרְמְיָ֣הוּ הַנָּבִ֑יא וַיִּתֵּ֨ן אֹתֹ֜ו עַל־הַמַּהְפֶּ֗כֶת אֲשֶׁ֨ר בְּשַׁ֤עַר בִּנְיָמִן֙ הָֽעֶלְיֹ֔ון אֲשֶׁ֖ר בְּבֵ֥ית יְהוָֽה׃
text.KJV JER 20:2: Then Pashur smote Jeremiah the prophet, and put him in the stocks that were in the high gate of Benjamin, which was by the house of the LORD.

B.name: Immer
B.line: Priest, father of Pashur the chief governor in Jeremiah's day
family: father-of pashhur-2 (Pashhur, son (descendant?) of Immer, chief officer in the Temple (JER)

why: The Hebrew identifies Pashhur as בֶּן־אִמֵּר, “son of Immer,” and describes Pashhur as a chief officer in the LORD’s house. This matches B’s stated relationship and setting; A is identified through Meshillemith and other priestly descendants.
